He was ranked among the top [[point guard]]s in the national class of 2015 by [[Rivals.com]], [[Scout.com]] and [[ESPN]]. He completed his senior year at [[Roselle Catholic High School]] in 2015, and then played two seasons of [[college basketball]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]]. ==Early life== [[File:20150401 MCDAAG Isaiah Briscoe in open space.JPG|150px|thumb|left|Briscoe in the 2015 McDonald's All-America game]] Briscoe was born in [[Union Township, Union County, New Jersey|Newark, New Jersey]]. He grew up in Newark until his later years when he moved to Union, New Jersey. His father, George Briscoe, is a hall of famer and former guard at [[Stockton State College]], his sister, Iasia Hemingway, played at [[Syracuse University]].{{cite web|url=http://blog.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2011/10/iasia_hemingways_little_brothe.html|title=Iasia Hemingway's little brother – Isaiah Briscoe – visits SU tonight, plus other Orange women notes|date=October 15, 2011}} When he was in seventh grade, he was not selected to an elite [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] team, which fueled his determination.{{cite news|last1=Jordan|first1=Jason|title=Isaiah Briscoe's on-court cockiness helps him consistently dominate|url=http://usatodayhss.com/2015/isaiah-briscoe-owns-his-on-court-cockiness-chalks-it-up-as-a-necessary-evil-isaiah-briscoe-kentucky-bbn-briscoe-must-see-tv-isaiah-briscoe-mcdonalds-all-american|access-date=June 23, 2015|work=[[USA Today]]|date=April 1, 2015}} After his eighth-grade year at Kawameeh Middle School in Union, Briscoe repeated the grade at Good Shepherd Academy in [[Irvington, New Jersey|Irvington]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nj.com/hssports/blog/boysbasketball/index.ssf/2013/07/staying_back_to_get_ahead_high_school_basketball_players_are_staying_back_in_middle_school_to_get_an.html |title=Staying back to get ahead: High school basketball players are repeating grades to get an edge}} He was invited to the [[LeBron James]] Skills Academy. Briscoe played well, using his body to get to the rim, he was advanced physically for his age. Briscoe was one of only three players from the 2015 class to be invited.{{cite web|url=http://pointguardu.com/lebron-james-skills-academy-notes/|title=LeBron James Skills Academy Notes|access-date=July 3, 2015|archive-date=July 5, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150705041406/http://pointguardu.com/lebron-james-skills-academy-notes/|url-status=dead}} After the eighth grade, He attended [[Saint Benedict's Preparatory School]]. He teamed with point guard [[Tyler Ennis (basketball)|Tyler Ennis]], to lead the Gray Bees to the brink of an [[ESPN]] National High School Invitational championship. They lost on a last-second 3-pointer to [[Montverde Academy]], 67–65. Briscoe had 11 points in the game. Isaiah averaged 15.1 points, 4.6 assists, 3.5 rebounds and 2.3 steals his sophomore season for the 32–2 Gray Bees.{{Cite web|url=http://zagsblog.com/articles/isaiah-briscoe-leaving-st-benedicts-prep/|title = Isaiah Briscoe Leaving St. Benedict's Prep (UPDATED)|date = June 12, 2013}} Briscoe transferred to [[Roselle Catholic High School]] for his junior year, where he was coached by Dave Boff. He led the team to state titles in 2014 and 2015, scoring 27 points in his final high school game to lead Roselle Catholic to a win in the state's overall [[Tournament of Champions (NJSIAA)|Tournament of Champions]].Dzenis, Brian. [https://www.trentonian.com/sports/roselle-catholic-takes-toc-title-over-pope-john/article_bd24e882-26e5-5b17-b95b-8a6ec925548d.html "Roselle Catholic takes TOC title over Pope John"], ''[[The Trentonian]]'', March 23, 2015. Accessed November 27, 2020. "This year’s Tournament of Champions ended the way most of these games have ended at this stage of the postseason: on an anticlimactic note. Roselle Catholic didn’t have its best game, but the effort was enough to beat Pope John, 57–45, Monday night at Trenton’s Sun National Bank Center. In the matchup between Kentucky-bound Isaiah Briscoe and Moustapha Diagne, who will be a future teammate of TCA’s Malachai Richardson at Syracuse, Briscoe showed why he caught the eye of John Calipari. He led Roselle with 27 points on the final night of his high school career." As a senior, Briscoe averaged 21 points, five rebounds and three assists per game. He models his game after [[Deron Williams]] and [[Tyreke Evans]].{{cite news|last1=Jones|first1=Steve|title=Briscoe hopes to continue line of Calipari pros|url=http://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/recruiting/kentucky/2015/01/21/briscoe-hopes-continue-line-calipari-pros/22135489/|access-date=June 23, 2015|work=[[The Courier-Journal]]|date=January 21, 2015}} Prior to his senior year, Briscoe led the [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] New Jersey Playaz to the championship at the 2014 [[Nike, Inc.|Nike]] Peach Jam in [[South Carolina]]. He posted averages of 19.2 points and 5 assists over 23 total games in the [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League]] (EYBL) in 2014. Isaiah finished as [[Rivals.com]] #10 nationally ranked player and the #1 point guard in the class of 2015.{{cite web|url=http://www.aseaofblue.com/2015-basketball-recruiting/2014/11/13/7217809/isaiah-briscoe-the-1-point-guard-in-2015-commits-to-the-kentucky|title=Isaiah Briscoe, the #1 Point Guard in 2015, Commits to the Kentucky Wildcats over UConn, St. Johns|first=Glenn|last=Logan|date=November 13, 2014}} He committed to Kentucky on November 13, 2014, live on [[ESPNU]], becoming the third highest ranked point guard that [[John Calipari]] signed at the school.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/11871615/skal-labissiere-isaiah-briscoe-commit-kentucky-wildcats|title=Kentucky gains 2015's top class|access-date=June 23, 2015|date=November 13, 2014|work=[[ESPN]]}} "(UK) puts me in the best position to play basketball after college," Briscoe said. "Calipari puts you on the highest stage. The last couple years, all his point guards have been in the NBA. I'm just trying to be the next one." He chose Kentucky over [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's]]. He was the nation's consensus top point guard, was ranked No. 13 overall player by [[ESPNU Recruiting Insider|ESPN]] and [[Scout.com|Scout]], No. 10 by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]], and No. 12 by 24/7 Sports recruiting services.{{cite web|url=http://www.scout.com/college/basketball/recruiting/topic/players?type=players&start=null&category=Basketball%20Recruiting&classYear=2015&minimumInterest=Low|title=2015 Basketball Recruiting Prospects|access-date=January 26, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160306125915/http://www.scout.com/college/basketball/recruiting/topic/players?type=players&start=null&category=Basketball%20Recruiting&classYear=2015&minimumInterest=Low|archive-date=March 6, 2016|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/playerrankings/_/class/2015/order/true|title=ESPN Basketball Recruiting – Player Rankings}}{{cite web|url=https://rivals.yahoo.com/basketballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/rankings/rank-3252|title=Yahoo Sports: Rivals.com Ranking – Class of 2015 Rivals150}}{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/Season/2015-Basketball/CompositeRecruitRankings/?InstitutionGroup=HighSchool|title=2015 Top Basketball Recruits}} He helped lead Team USA at the 2014 FIBA Americans U18 Championships to a gold medal.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/111414aaa.html|title=Kentucky Adds Three for 2015|access-date=June 23, 2015|date=November 14, 2014|publisher=University of Kentucky|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150412181802/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/111414aaa.html|archive-date=April 12, 2015|url-status=dead}} He was a first-team [[Parade All-American]] in 2015. He was a [[McDonald's All-American Game]], [[Jordan Brand Classic]], and [[Nike Hoop Summit]] game selection.{{cite news|url=http://www.kentucky.com/2015/01/28/3665975/uk-signee-briscoe-named-mcdonalds.html|title=UK signees Briscoe, Murray named McDonald's All-Americans|access-date=June 23, 2014|date=January 28, 2015|work=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]]}}{{cite news|url=http://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/recruiting/2015/03/05/jordan-games-uk-signees/24428427/|title=Four UK signees chosen to Jordan Brand Classic|access-date=June 23, 2015|date=March 5, 2015|work=[[The Courier-Journal]]}}{{cite web|url=http://highschoolsports.nj.com/news/article/-6431054006329901547/boys-basketball-roselle-catholics-isaiah-briscoe-named-to-nike-hoops-summit-roster/|title=Boys Basketball: Roselle Catholic's Isaiah Briscoe named to Nike Hoops Summit roster|date=February 2, 2015}} ==College career== [[File:Isaiah-Briscoe-2.jpg|150px|thumb|left|Briscoe in Kentucky's 2016 Blue-White scrimmage]] As a freshman, Briscoe averaged 9.6 points and 5.3 rebounds per game. However, he struggled with his shooting particularly from outside, hitting only 14 percent of his attempts from behind the arc. Coming into his sophomore season, he worked at playing more of a point guard role.{{cite news |last1=Graves |first1=Gary |title=Kentucky basketball: Isaiah Briscoe looks to improve shooting, leadership |url=https://www.ncaa.com/news/basketball-men/article/2016-06-16/kentucky-basketball-isaiah-briscoe-looks-improve-shooting |access-date=June 10, 2018 |work=NCAA.com |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=June 16, 2016}} He posted 12.1 points, 5.4 rebounds, and 4.2 assists per game as a sophomore.{{cite news |last1=Camerato |first1=Jessica |title=Sixers' 1st pre-draft workouts include Philly native, plenty of guards |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/tags/isaiah-briscoe |access-date=June 10, 2018 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=June 3, 2017}} At the conclusion of his sophomore season, Briscoe announced that he would forgo his final two years of collegiate eligibility and enter the [[2017 NBA draft]] joining teammates [[De'Aaron Fox]], [[Malik Monk]], and [[Bam Adebayo]] becoming the fourth Kentucky Wildcat to do so.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/19092075/isaiah-briscoe-becomes-fourth-kentucky-wildcats-player-declare-nba-draft|title=Kentucky's Isaiah Briscoe declares for NBA draft|website=[[ESPN]]|author=Jeff Goodman|date=April 6, 2017|access-date=April 6, 2017}} ==Professional career== ===Kalev/Cramo (2017–2018)=== After going undrafted in the [[2017 NBA draft]], Briscoe joined the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] for the [[2017 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|last=Marcum|first=Jason|url=https://www.aseaofblue.com/2017/6/23/15860306/isaiah-briscoe-joining-76ers-nba-summer-league|title=Isaiah Briscoe joining 76ers for NBA Summer League|work=aseaofblue.com|date=June 23, 2017|access-date=July 1, 2017}} In six games for the 76ers, he averaged 5.5 points and 2.2 assists per game. On September 14, 2017, he signed a training camp contract with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-sign-isaiah-briscoe/|title=TRAIL BLAZERS SIGN ISAIAH BRISCOE|work=NBA.com|date=September 14, 2017|access-date=October 31, 2017}} He was waived by the Trail Blazers on October 13, 2017, after appearing in six preseason games.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-waive-briscoe-goodwin-and-morrow/|title=TRAIL BLAZERS WAIVE BRISCOE, GOODWIN AND MORROW|work=NBA.com|date=October 13, 2017|access-date=October 31, 2017}} Briscoe signed with Estonian club [[BC Kalev|Kalev/Cramo]]. On February 16, 2018, Briscoe scored 50 points as he took home MVP honors at the Estonia/Latvia All Star Game. On June 9, 2018, Briscoe won the [[VTB United League Young Player of the Year]] award, given to the league's best player under age 23. In the 2017–18 season Briscoe averaged 18.5 points, 3.4 rebounds, 4.2 assists, and 1.6 steals in 26.7 minutes per game. ===Orlando Magic (2018–2019)=== On July 6, 2018, Briscoe signed with the [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite web|title=RELEASE: Magic Sign Briscoe|url=https://twitter.com/Magic_PR/status/1015301987943018497|website=Magic PR on Twitter|date=July 6, 2018|access-date=July 9, 2018}}{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-sign-isaiah-briscoe-20180706|title=Magic Sign Isaiah Briscoe|work=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2018|access-date=July 9, 2018}} He made his NBA debut
